scope: development tooling: exact worker-wrapper identity predicate for supervisor capacity scanning and launch recovery

source.delivery_head_binding: The governed handoff freezes the PR head containing this manifest; implementation_commit is its source ancestor.

problem.summary: Two independent live audits found the scheduler identified a live worker_runner.py wrapper with a raw substring search ("worker_runner.py" in the whole /proc/<pid>/cmdline text) instead of an exact argv-path predicate. Provider CLI and bwrap sandbox descendants inherit the wake prompt as an argv value; when that inherited prompt text itself contains the literal string "worker_runner.py" (for example while quoting the task's own artifact path), the substring search matched the descendant too. An earlier candidate replaced this with a loose argv[0:4] check, but independent reproduction showed that provider arguments (e.g. claude --prompt /repo/.../worker_runner.py) and bubblewrap bind operands (bwrap --ro-bind /repo/.../worker_runner.py) were still mistakenly matched as worker wrappers. A subsequent review reproduction also revealed that generic dash-option parsing allowed non-wrapper Python invocations like clustered/attached inline code (-uc<code>) and stdin mode (-) to match when worker_runner.py appeared as a downstream option/operand. The predicate must parse Python CLI options conservatively and reject non-script modes.

fix.predicate: supervisor.py defines cmdline_is_worker_runner, binding directly to the actual interpreter or direct script invocation instead of accepting any matching path token in argv[0:4]. For direct invocation, argv[0] must be worker_runner.py under .orchestrator. For Python interpreter invocation, argv[0] must be a Python/PyPy executable, followed by optional Python interpreter flags (conservatively parsed, respecting option arguments like -W/-X and excluding stdin mode - and clustered/attached -c/-m), and the first positional script argument must be worker_runner.py under .orchestrator. Provider CLI arguments (claude --prompt ...), bubblewrap mount operands (bwrap --ro-bind ...), inline code (-c), module execution (-m), and stdin mode (-) are rejected.
unchanged: zombie/dead-process filtering (Z/X state check, pid_is_alive gate)

run-id handling, lease behavior, promotion-drain behavior

acceptance_evidence.exact_predicate: Both scan_live_worker_pids_by_agent and _proc_worker_runner_launch_marker use the tightened cmdline_is_worker_runner predicate bound to the actual interpreter/script invocation.
acceptance_evidence.focused_regressions: test_scan_live_worker_pids_excludes_prompt_text_and_bwrap_descendants proves supported wrapper invocations (standard python3, python3 -u, direct script execution) are counted while provider arguments (claude --prompt), bwrap bind operands (bwrap --ro-bind), prompt text references, python running unrelated scripts, inline code (-c, -uc), stdin mode (-), and non-.orchestrator scripts are excluded. test_proc_worker_runner_launch_marker_rejects_descendants_and_bind_operands proves launch recovery rejects provider arguments, bwrap operands, inline code (-uc), and stdin mode (-) even when ORCH_TASK_ID, ORCH_AGENT_ID, and ORCH_RUN_ID match in environ. test_proc_worker_runner_launch_marker_recovers_real_wrapper provides positive recovery coverage for a real python wrapper. test_cmdline_is_worker_runner_predicate_supported_and_rejected directly unit tests the predicate against supported and rejected options.
acceptance_evidence.preserved_behavior: Pre-existing test_zombie_worker_pid_treated_as_non_live_and_does_not_block_dispatch continues to pass unchanged; full test_supervisor.py and test_supervisor_watchdog.py suites pass with 402 tests and 98 subtests green.
acceptance_evidence.documentation: docs/operations/supervisor-worker-identity.md records the identity rule, interpreter/script binding, procfs boundaries, relation between watchdog and scheduler counts, and the reproducible timestamped runtime health/count observation.
acceptance_evidence.delivery_scope: Only the declared tooling files (.orchestrator/supervisor.py, .orchestrator/test_supervisor.py, docs/operations/supervisor-worker-identity.md, this evidence file) changed; no product runtime behavior, hosted deployment, external branch protection, task state, or unrelated worktree was touched.
